The Jewish people see themselves as separate and distinct from others, so they would not have betrayed Jesus. Remember that James the just, brother of Jesus, stayed in Jerusalem protected by Jewish authorities after Jesus died. This makes no sense if Jesus' teachings went against Jewish law, which led to his execution by Jewish priests.

The Romans are brutal; they killed people for any reason. So it's more likely the Romans killed Jesus for their own reasons rather than Jews. The Bible says the Jews conspired against Jesus and encouraged the Romans to kill him, but I'm not convinced of this. 

Why did the Jews conspire against Jesus? The story is not true. If Jesus was divine, how could he die? Why does death have meaning? What about the resurrection and second coming? These questions are raised in other religions but not in others. Christians explain it as a miracle, mystery, or magic; just believe it.

In our class, we question everything. We ask who Jesus is and what he believed. The first question is what did Jesus teach? He probably didn't preach that you'll be saved if you follow him. Why was he popular? What made his beliefs appealing?

Why did the Romans kill him? These are three big questions: what he taught, why he was popular, and whether the Romans killed him. My argument is that Jesus taught what every poet-prophet we studied this semester taught—about a source emanating to create the universe, with souls coming from it. This cycle continues until merging back into the source. 

Jesus' teachings were for his time, but why is he special? The Roman Empire was particularly evil.
